terms.gloss: local, native, home-grown (of produce, breeds and words)
evidence: Varr. LL 5.77: aquātilium vocābula partim sunt vernācula partim peregrīna (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “native, domestic, indigenous”, the classical sense, as against peregrīnus, foreign: local hens and vines, local names. Morgan–Owens gives it for “local”, and ferculum vernāculum for a local speciality.

terms.register: vōx ut adjectīvum plērumque poētica: Hor., Verg., Ov.; in ōrātiōne solūtā Liv.
evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.14.24: nec vīcīna subest vīnum praebēre taberna
terms.comment: The shop or the tavern round the corner. As an adjective mostly poetic (Lewis & Short); in prose vīcīnus is mostly the noun, a neighbour (see neighbour), and the local people are the vīcīnitās (see community).

evidence: Traupman 341: numerus locālis, a local telephone number
terms.comment: Late Latin; Traupman uses it for a local call. Classical Latin says vernāculus or vīcīnus.

phrases.latin: nec vīcīna subest vīnum praebēre taberna quae possit tibi
phrases.english: and there is no tavern nearby that could serve you wine

phrases.latin: vernācula: lactūca ā lacte, quod holus id habet lac
phrases.english: native plants: lettuce, lactūca, from lac, milk, because the plant has milk in it

sources: Lewis & Short: vernaculus · Lewis & Short: vicinus · Lewis & Short: localis
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. local.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 341.
